**EDG/USDT pair:**

**Buy and Sell total  396629.063311$**
**Sell value total  197836.604284$**
**Buy value total  198792.459028$**

	![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/bxSZn7sO2kuPLcdKCQ9Kk7RjaX5Qx7UHnl94A2QscLhy_yB7v26QMZNXqiBq6ljNPwdWLR02Yu5L1cOgdzzv_H8z4CZ-OT5a1y4SjvRE3NgG2zJ0gnsHLmoaRPszCkhA_hY_JkCTSEiMIDNkcw0y-ej2CVE82bcPd2jfl1hvAlFi5YkSY14lqc4tJZByRg)


So looking at the above numbers we can see that the burn rate comes to about ~8000$ per month per pair. Considering the current market situation, the above mentioned strategies can be slightly tweaked towards the passive side in order to reduce the burn rate, thus helping the inventory to sustain longer.

**Possible Passive Strategies:**

1. Order_Amount per order:

	HummingBot allows setting the EDG deployed per order using order_amount parameter. Considering the fact that we need to take a passive approach, the amount can be reduced compared to the current rate.

2. Hanging_orders:
	In the last phase, we were actively using the hanging orders feature provided by Humingbot. This helped us to keep individual order in a pair active, when the corresponding order is triggered. The details have been discussed in the main post. In the passive strategy, we would not be using this feature and prefer the default orders version.

3.  Ask/Bid spreads:
	Our previous requirement was to fulfill the Kucoin Exchange’s terms and condition to avoid the ST tag. Considering this fact, we had to keep the spreads very tight in order to execute the majority of the orders and have the volume levels up to the mark. In this phase, we will have to relax those spreads upto an extent and tighten them only when natural volumes are absent.

4.  Switching On/Off of the bot in intervals:
	Another strategy that we can follow is to completely switch off the bot during the occurrence of periods of sustained natural volumes. We will need to do the monitoring of these occurrences and preserve the inventory.


**The way forward:**

The following thoughts and suggestions were discussed in multiple calls.
Considering the market situation we are currently in as well as considering the EDG treasury status, appointing an external Market Maker to carry out this activity in conjunction with the DFS team or alone won’t be feasible. The reason for this is that professional Market Makers demand a significant inventory on either side to carry out their task efficiently. So, we the DFS team would continue to provide the services for the month of Jan/Feb’22 at a very subsidized cost, which will be inline with the decision of the other SCU members/contributors. Another point that was suggested was to do the Market Making only for the EDG/USDT pair, considering it's the most commonly traded.

Considering the burn rate, our ask would be for 5k USD equivalent amount on each side. Our approach will be to try and reduce the burn rate and use the amount for 2 months of Market Making.

Hey DFS - thanks for sharing this.

It makes sense to try this - I guess my main question is who are you market making for and whether this can also be framed as helping to enable contributors to liquidate funds in a more efficient manner than market selling which is something I've had to do at various points.

I can see this makes sense to ensure our status on Kucoin, but I'd be interested if you could maybe outline how this internal capability could be a useful resource on the contributor side, rather than using it to generate fees.

This feels like a productive use, rather than a more general one if that makes sense and can be applied to other grass-roots networks (Kabocha etc)

Hey Rich!
This initiative was primarily started due to Kucoin requirements, but along with that it indirectly also helps contributors like all of us to liquidate our incentives in a much more efficient manner i.e. w/o affecting the prices significantly.
For the past couple of weeks, we've been running the MM actively and we can see the volumes are significantly up compared to the previous 2 months(Sept/Oct). These volumes may not have been entirely contributed by the MM service, but it played a huge role in providing the much needed impetus, which indicates activity to traders and then they add to the trading activity.
How this helps contributors? We can liquidate their incentives relatively easily, because now there is a larger scope to absorb these volumes. Though our strong suggestions, to all the contributors would be avoid **using Market orders and instead use Limit Orders**, which can help the markets to easily absorb the volumes. In the future, when we have a bigger inventory, the order sizes of the bots will be relatively bigger and can significantly help in absorbing these volumes. Thus, its a win-win!
